lesson.child_mission: Digital time shows hours and minutes with a colon (for example 09:05). Match digital displays to analog clock faces in 12-hour time.
lesson.evidence_instructions: Save the independent response, specific revisions and both short-answer explanations; record oral evidence for speaking tasks.
lesson.extension: Apply the same method to a larger number or a new context, then compare two solution paths for accuracy.
lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Write digital for: minute hand on 2, hour near 7. Draw analog for 4:50.

FEEDBACK
7:10; analog with minute on 10, hour near 5.

WATCH FOR
Writing 7:70 as a time is impossible — minutes only go 00–59.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Match ten digital↔analog pairs. Convert eight times both ways. Correct three invalid digital times and write why each fails.

Write a short reflection naming one step you corrected and why.
lesson.learning_intention: Digital time shows hours and minutes with a colon (for example 09:05). Match digital displays to analog clock faces in 12-hour time.
materials: Optional: place-value chart or number line
lesson.offline_alternative: Use paper and pencil to complete the original task, then retain a photograph or short parent observation as evidence.
lesson.parent_notes:
Parent: Marking guidance for the independent task: Match ten digital↔analog pairs. Convert eight times both ways. Correct three invalid digital times and write why each fails. Accept equivalent original responses that show the same skill.

Parent: Written model 1: Sample: new numbers solved with visible working for digital; key places/values named. Do not award marks for retyping the model.

Parent: Written model 2: Sample misconception: Writing 7:70 as a time is impossible — minutes only go 00–59.. Correction uses 7:10; analog with minute on 10, hour near 5.. Why: restores accurate digital.

Parent: Likely misconception: Writing 7:70 as a time is impossible — minutes only go 00–59. Keep sample answers out of the child role.

Parent: Short-answer focus 1: Solve one fresh problem that uses digital with different numbers from the worked model. Show working and name the places or values that matter.

Parent: Short-answer focus 2: Describe one likely mistake with digital, show corrected working, and say why the correction works.

Parent: Marking notes: Accept any mathematically valid solution that uses new numbers, shows working for digital, and names places/values. Reject copied model numbers. / Accept a named misconception about digital, corrected working, and a method reason. Reject vague “I was wrong” with no repair..

WORKED MODEL
2:45 digital matches an analog clock with minute hand on 9 (45 minutes) and hour hand near 3. 09:05 means 9 hours and 5 minutes.

TRY FIRST
Write digital for: minute hand on 2, hour near 7. Draw analog for 4:50.

FEEDBACK
7:10; analog with minute on 10, hour near 5.
teach_steps.explain:
Digital time shows hours and minutes with a colon (for example 09:05). Match digital displays to analog clock faces in 12-hour time.

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner choose methods based on place value, quantity and accurate working, rather than guessing digits by shape alone. Keep every step justified.

HOW TO WORK
Read the worked example and name the places, values or distances that carry the method. Before looking at the correction, make your own attempt using the exact question provided. Compare your working with the feedback: did you use the same skill and show your reasoning? If a digit or place is uncertain, identify what would have to be regrouped or counted again. One deliberate, justified revision is more useful than writing a longer answer.
